'''Horaisan Kofun''' (also '''Horai-yama Kofun''' or '''Horai-zan Kofun'''{{Sfn|Horai-yama Kofun (Tomb Mound)|1989}}) is an ancient [[tomb mound]] located in {{ill|Den-en-chōfu|fa|دن-ئن-چوفو|fi|Den'enchōfu|fr|Den-en-chōfu|ja|田園調布|ko|덴엔초후|nl|Den-en-chōfu|ru|Дэнъэнтёфу|zh|田園調布|qid=Q2613265}}, [[Ota, Tokyo|Ota Ward]], [[Tokyo]]. Its shape is that of a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} (keyhole-shaped tomb). It is one of the tomb mounds constituting the {{ill|Ebaradai kofun-gun|ja|荏原台古墳群|qid=Q11618305}} (Ebara Tomb Mound Cluster). It is designated as a Tokyo Metropolitan Historic Site.

== Overview ==
Located in southern Tokyo, this is a large keyhole-shaped tomb mound constructed on the edge of a terrace on the left bank of the {{ill|Tama River|ja|多摩川}} in the southwestern part of the {{ill|Musashino Plateau|ja|武蔵野台地}}. The {{ill|Ebaradai kofun-gun|ja|荏原台古墳群|qid=Q11618305}} (Ebara Tomb Mound Cluster) was built on this plateau, and this tomb mound, together with {{ill|Kamezukayama Kofun|ja|亀甲山古墳}} (a national [[historic site]]), represents the Ebaradai Tomb Mound Cluster. The tomb name "Horai" is a name that has been used since ancient times<ref group="note">Regarding the tomb name "Horai," the earliest usage is said to be the place name "Horai" on the 1906 (Meiji 39) Land Survey Department map "Mizokuchi." In the 1992 Tokyo Metropolitan cultural properties catalog, it was listed as "Horai-yama Kofun," but with the change from Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Relic to Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Site in 1996, it was changed to "Horaisan Kofun."</ref>. In [[1934]] (Showa 9), two-thirds of the rear circular section was lost due to soil extraction, at which time the burial facility was exposed and grave goods were excavated{{Sfn|Horaisan Kofun (Heibonsha)|2002}}<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>. The remaining parts of the tumulus are well preserved<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>, and a confirmation survey was conducted in [[1995]] (Heisei 7)<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/><ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>.

The tumulus shape is a keyhole shape with the front section spreading outward in a fan shape<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/><ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>, with the front section oriented to the southeast to face {{ill|Kamezukayama Kofun|ja|亀甲山古墳}}{{Sfn|Horaisan Kofun (Heibonsha)|2002}}<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/>. The tumulus has three tiers in the rear circular section and two tiers in the front section<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/><ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>. {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}} (stone paving) and {{ill|haniwa|ja|埴輪}} have not been identified on the exterior surface of the tumulus{{Sfn|Horai-yama Kofun (Tomb Mound)|1989}}, and a single-tier terrace surrounds the tumulus<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/><ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>. The burial facility is a {{ill|clay vault|ja|粘土槨}} located 3 meters below the summit of the rear circular section, and numerous grave goods were excavated when it was discovered<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>. The existence of another burial facility in the front section is also presumed (details unknown as it has not been investigated)<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo"/><ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>. The construction period is estimated to be the late [[4th century]]<ref name="Display explanation"/> (or early 4th century in the early Kofun period<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>) in the middle Kofun period, predating the construction of {{ill|Kamezukayama Kofun|ja|亀甲山古墳}}<ref name="Display explanation"/>, and it is positioned as the first chieftain's tomb in the lower {{ill|Tama River|ja|多摩川}} basin<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>.

The tomb mound area was designated as a Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Relic in [[1955]] (Showa 30), and was redesignated as a Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Site in [[1996]] (Heisei 8)<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>. The surrounding area is currently maintained as a historic site within {{ill|Tamagawadai Park|ja|多摩川台公園}}.

== Site History ==
* [[1934]] (Showa 9): Soil extraction during residential land development. Discovery of burial facility and excavation of grave goods<ref>[http://www.city.ota.tokyo.jp/shisetsu/rekishi/minemachi_denenchoufu/houraiyama_kofun.html Horai-yama Kofun] (Ota Ward website).</ref>.
* [[1955]] (Showa 30) March 28: Designated as Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Relic<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>.
* [[1995]] (Heisei 7): Confirmation survey accompanying park development<ref name="Explanation board Tokyo">Historic site explanation board (Tokyo Metropolitan Board of Education, installed 1998).</ref>.
* [[1996]] (Heisei 8) March 18: Type changed to Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Site<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>.

== Tumulus ==
The dimensions of the tumulus are as follows<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>:
* Tumulus length: 97.5 meters
* Rear circular section - Three-tier construction. Two-thirds lost due to leveling.
** Diameter: 52 meters
** Height: 11 meters
* Front section - Two-tier construction.
** Width: 37 meters
** Height: 8 meters

== Excavated Items ==
[[File:宝萊山古墳 出土品.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Excavated items}}{{small|Displayed at Ota Ward Folk Museum.}}]]
The grave goods excavated from the burial facility are as follows<ref name="Display explanation">Display explanation at Ota Ward Tamagawadai Park Tomb Mound Exhibition Room (as of November 2017).</ref>:
* Imitation Four-Beast Mirror: 1
* Spindle whorl-shaped jasper artifact: 1
* Magatama (curved jewels): 4
* Kudatama (tubular beads): 67
* Marutama (round beads): 173
* Kodama (small beads): 391
* Large swords: 10
* Spears (spear-shaped iron implements): 2
* Small knives: 1
These excavated items are currently stored at [[Keio University]] and the Ota Ward Folk Museum (5-chome Minami-Magome, Ota Ward), and replicas are displayed at the Ota Ward Tamagawadai Park Tomb Mound Exhibition Room<ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Historic Site
** Horaisan Kofun - Marker installed April 1926 (Taisho 15), designated as historic site April 1, 1952 (Showa 27), designated as historic relic March 28, 1955 (Showa 30), type changed March 18, 1996 (Heisei 8)<ref name="Tokyo Metro">[http://bunkazai.metro.tokyo.jp/jp/search_detail.html?page=1&id=536 Horaisan Kofun] (Tokyo Metropolitan Board of Education Regional Education Support Division "Tokyo Metropolitan Cultural Properties Information Database").</ref>.

== Site Information ==
'''Location'''
* 4-4-1 {{ill|Den-en-chōfu|fa|دن-ئن-چوفو|fi|Den'enchōfu|fr|Den-en-chōfu|ja|田園調布|ko|덴엔초후|nl|Den-en-chōfu|ru|Дэнъэnтёфу|zh|田園調布|qid=Q2613265}}, [[Ota, Tokyo|Ota Ward]], [[Tokyo]] (within {{ill|Tamagawadai Park|ja|多摩川台公園}})

'''Entry to the site'''
* The tomb mound area is surrounded by a fence but entry is possible during the day; it is locked only at night, restricting entry.

'''Transportation Access'''
* {{ill|Tokyu Corporation|ja|東急電鉄}} {{ill|Toyoko Line|ja|東急東横線}}・{{ill|Meguro Line|ja|東急目黒線}}・{{ill|Tamagawa Line|ja|東急多摩川線}} {{ill|Tamagawa Station|ja|多摩川駅}} (approximately 15-minute walk)<ref name="Tokyo Metro"/>

'''Related Facilities'''
* [[Keio University]] - Stores original excavated items from Horaisan Kofun<ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>.
* Ota Ward Folk Museum (5-chome Minami-Magome, Ota Ward) - Stores original excavated items from Horaisan Kofun<ref name="Explanation board Ota">Historic site explanation board (installed by Ota Ward).</ref>.
* Ota Ward Tamagawadai Park Tomb Mound Exhibition Room (1-chome Den-en-chofu, Ota Ward) - Guidance facility for tomb mounds in Tamagawadai Park. Displays replicas of excavated items from Horaisan Kofun<ref name="Explanation board Ota"/>.

'''Vicinity'''
* {{ill|Ebaradai kofun-gun|ja|荏原台古墳群|qid=Q11618305}}
** {{ill|Kamezukayama Kofun|ja|亀甲山古墳}} - National historic site.
** Tamagawadai Tomb Mound Cluster - Tokyo Metropolitan Designated Historic Site. A late-period tomb mound cluster constructed between {{ill|Kamezukayama Kofun|ja|亀甲山古墳}} and Horaisan Kofun.
